text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- West Bank wave of arrests continues; about 30 Hamas and Islamic Jihad activists detained.
- Treasury chiefs to present prime minister with proposal for further budget cuts.
- Two border policemen who beat Palestinians under arrest and interrogated by unit that investigates police.
- Treasury chief Meridor to present today to Prime Minister Netanyahu a proposal for additional cut of 2.25 billion shekels in 1997 budget.
MAARIV
- Fears that Hebron talks could collapse.
- Economic officials say no choice but to raise taxes and perhaps VAT.
- Senior official says situation on Syrian border has calmed.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Treasury preparing painful cuts in welfare and education budgets.
- Palestinian President Arafat, heading to donors' meeting in Paris, waited hours for Israel to give his helicopter clearance to fly from Gaza to Egypt yesterday.
GLOBES
- Netanyahu to Likud party forum: "If we don't cut at least six billion to seven billion shekels from the budget, the economy will collapse."
- Treasury chief Meridor says additional budget cut needed for 1997 but hasn't decided on a date.
- Netanyahu to try to persuade Orbit to cancel its decision not to build a plant in Eilat.
JERUSALEM POST
- Senior government official: Defence budget safe from extra cuts.
- Defence chief Mordechai: Despite arrests, threat of suicide attacks still exists.
- Detained border policemen may face criminal charges.
- Netanyahu: Full Israeli army access in Hebron is a must.
- Mordechai to discuss weapons sales with Britain.
